The graph represents the function $y=\frac{a}{x}+k.$ What are the values of $a$ and $k?$

$a=$

{{field-2}}
questions.worked_solution:
First, notice that the horizontal asymptote of the graph is $y=1.$ This means that $k=1$ and we can re-write our function as

$$
y=\frac{a}{x}+1.
$$

Also, we are given that the point $(1,3.5)$ lies on the graph. Substituting its coordinates into the equation above, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =\frac{a}{x}+1 \\ 3.5 & =\frac{a}{1}+1 \\ 3.5 & =a+1 \\ a & =2.5.\end{aligned}
$$

The graph represents the function $y=\frac{a}{x-b}+k.$ What are the values of $a,$ $b,$ and $k?$

questions.worked_solution:
First, notice that the horizontal asymptote of the graph is $y=2.5,$ while the vertical asymptote is $x=-2.$ This means that $k=2.5$ and $b=-2,$ and we can re-write our function as

$$
y=\frac{a}{x-(-2)}+2.5=\frac{a}{x+2}+2.5.
$$

Also, we are given that the point $(-5,3.5)$ lies on the graph. Substituting its coordinates into the equation above, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =\frac{a}{x+2}+2.5 \\ 3.5 & =\frac{a}{-5+2}+2.5 \\ 1 & =\frac{a}{(-3)} \\ a & =-3.\end{aligned}
$$

First, notice that the horizontal asymptote of the graph is $y=1.5.$ This means that $k=1.5$ and we can re-write our function as

y=\frac{a}{x}+1.5.

Also, we are given that the point $(1,3.5)$ lies on the graph. Substituting its coordinates into the equation above, we obtain

The graph represents the function $y=\frac{a}{x-b}+k.$ What is the value of $a+b+k?$
questions.worked_solution:
First, notice that the horizontal asymptote of the graph is $y=0.5,$ while the vertical asymptote is $x=3.$ This means that $k=0.5$ and $b=3,$ and we can re-write our function as

$$
y=\frac{a}{x-3}+0.5.
$$

Also, we are given that the point $(1,1.5)$ lies on the graph. Substituting its coordinates into the equation above, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =\frac{a}{x-3}+0.5 \\ 1.5 & =\frac{a}{1-3}+0.5 \\ 1 & =\frac{a}{-2} \\ a & =-2.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, $a+b+k=-2+3+0.5=1.5.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13831126/assets/fb46d056a8d8010eca509543c231c875f4980a21f1af17505fa98c8c64106207.png)

The diagram above shows the graph of $y = \dfrac{a}{x-b}+k.$ What is the value of $a+b+k?$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
First, notice that the horizontal asymptote of the graph is $y=-1,$ while the vertical asymptote is $x=2.$ This means that $k=-1$ and $b=2,$ and we can re-write our function as

$$
y = \dfrac{a}{x-2}+(-1) = \dfrac{a}{x-2}-1.
$$

Also, we are given that the point $(3,2)$ lies on the graph. Substituting its coordinates into the equation above, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =\frac{a}{x-2}-1 \\ 2 & =\frac{a}{3-2}-1 \\ 3 & =\frac{a}{1} \\ a & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, $a+b+k = 3+2+(-1) = 4.$
